what: Domino's Pizza is the world's largest pizza chain by sales. It owns few restaurants: franchisees run almost all of them, and Domino's earns royalties and sells them dough, cheese and equipment through its own supply chain.
customers: Franchisees, who pay royalties and buy supplies, and ultimately the customers ordering delivery and carryout.
money: dough, cheese and equipment sold to franchisees
United States franchise royalties and fees
royalties on franchisee sales plus advertising fees
the small number of stores it runs itself
moat: A delivery network of over 21,000 stores and an ordering technology stack built over two decades, which lets it deliver faster and cheaper than any single-market competitor.
risks: $5.0B of debt against $126M of cash, the result of years of borrowing to buy back shares
Delivery apps have given every local pizzeria a delivery capability Domino's used to own alone
The analyst average target is roughly where the shares trade
opportunities: 19 times earnings with $636M of free cash flow and a 12.2% net margin
The franchise model means revenue grows without Domino's spending on new stores
International store count keeps growing and carries royalty revenue at almost no cost
watch: United States same-store sales and net store openings worldwide.
